Title: Off-by-One Buffer Overflow (Out-of-Bounds Write) in lwm2m_engine.c
Analysis:
An off-by-one buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write) exists in `lwm2m_engine_start` of `subsys/net/lib/lwm2m/lwm2m_engine.c`. The function fetches the Security Object's Server URI string via `lwm2m_get_res_buf()`, which returns the string and its length `url_len` as stored in the resource database. If a string is written up to the maximum capacity `SECURITY_URI_LEN` (255 bytes) of the underlying static resource buffer `security_uri`, `url_len` is returned as 255. The statement `url[url_len] = '\0'` then writes a null terminator at `url[255]`, which is index 255 (the 256th byte) of a 255-byte array. This causes a one-byte out-of-bounds write on the contiguous static variables (corrupting adjacent memory, such as the `client_identity` array).

Conceptual Payload:
A remote bootstrap server or malicious actor writes a server URI string of length 255 to Object 0, Instance 0, Resource 0. When the client invokes `lwm2m_engine_start()`, `url_len` is 255. The client writes to `url[255]`, writing a null byte past the end of the `security_uri[0]` static buffer and into `client_identity[0]`.

Title: Out-of-Bounds Read via Non-Null-Terminated String in Pull Context
Analysis:
An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in `lwm2m_pull_context_start_transfer` within `subsys/net/lib/lwm2m/lwm2m_pull_context.c`. When starting a firmware transfer, the function copies the package URI into `context.uri` using `memcpy(context.uri, uri, LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN)`. Since `context.uri` is a character array of size `LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN`, if the untrusted package URI resource value is configured to be exactly `LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` bytes or more, the copied string will not be null-terminated. Subsequent usages, such as calling `strlen(context.uri)` or invoking `http_parser_parse_url()`, will read past the end of the `context.uri` array, causing an out-of-bounds memory read (potentially leading to a crash or information disclosure).

Conceptual Payload:
A malicious LwM2M server or bootstrap server writes a firmware package URI string of exactly `LWM2M_PACKAGE_URI_LEN` (e.g. 255) bytes into resource 5/0/1. When starting the firmware transfer, `lwm2m_pull_context_start_transfer` copies all 255 bytes via `memcpy` without a null terminator. Subsequent calls to `strlen(context.uri)` will continue reading until a null byte is found in memory, leading to out-of-bounds memory access.
